strategies.name: Sequential All-Reduce Chain (Baseline)
strategies.desc: Execute 8 dependent all-reduce operations sequentially, each followed by local elementwise operations (division, mean computation, vector arithmetic). This is the reference implementation with 8 all-reduce dispatches and minimal local compute fusion. Represents the straightforward approach with highest dispatch overhead but simplest structure.

strategies.name: Fused Local Computation Between Collectives
strategies.desc: Keep 8 all-reduce operations but fuse all local elementwise operations (u*mean(v*s), division by W, buffer construction) into minimal kernel launches between collectives. Reduces local compute overhead by batching vector operations and reusing computed u, v masks. Same 8 collective dispatches but lower host-device synchronization cost.

strategies.name: Chunked Vector All-Reduce Parallelism
strategies.desc: Partition the 16384-element vector into independent chunks (e.g., 4 chunks of 4096 elements) and pipeline the 8-iteration algorithm across chunks using non-blocking all-reduce operations where dependencies permit. Exploits potential parallelism in communication for different data segments. Total dispatches increase to ~32 but allows overlap of communication and computation across chunks.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with a reduce-scatter followed by all-gather pattern, computing the local operations only on the scattered partition (1/224th of data per rank). Reduces per-rank computation cost for mean and vector operations by 224x. Results in 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but dramatically lower local compute and memory bandwidth requirements.

strategies.name: Recursive Halving with Local Accumulation
strategies.desc:
Exploit the iterative structure by maintaining partial results in a local accumulator and using butterfly/recursive-halving all-reduce topology instead of ring-based. Pre-compute and cache u, v patterns and their products. Combines multiple buffer transformations into single kernels. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but optimizes network topology efficiency and eliminates redundant mask recomputation across iterations.
